result.rationale: Verifiable from the diff: `[z.string().toString()]` used as computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema produces '[object Object]' (z.string() is a ZodString object, not a string), collapsing the two computed keys into one and leaving only access_token required; zod strips unknown keys by default, so expiry_date/refresh_token are stripped; the new file then assigns the literal string "refresh_token" when the key is missing (`refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`), and this placeholder gets persisted via prisma.credential.update in the Google/Salesforce/Zoom call sites show

Schema selection depends only on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED + env var, not which refresh path ran, matching the described data-loss scenario.

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse's minimum schema is broken: z.string().toString() evaluates to '[object Object]', collapsing both computed keys into one meaningless property so the schema only requires access_token, and since zod strips unknown keys by default, every other token-response field (including expiry_date and the real refresh_token) is stripped; lines 22-24 then write the literal string 'refresh_token' into the parsed data whenever it's missing. Because the schema is selected purely on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT rather than which refresh path actually ran, team-owned Google/Zoom/O365 credentials get their real refresh tokens overwritten with the literal 'refresh_token' and persisted (silent data loss requiring re-auth), Salesforce token responses lose instance_url/signature before being persisted (breaking the jsforce connection), and even in the intended sync path all credentials get a placeholder refresh token, bricking every OAuth credential if sharing is later disabled.
